title: The Borrowed Uniform
premise: In the river town of Vellmere, on the eve of the Vellish uprising, Lior Crane has survived seven years in her father's print shop by learning which silences keep people safe—especially as a girl passing as a boy to keep her dead brother's apprenticeship. When imperial soldiers requisition the town and seize the master ledger holding every name, debt, and secret in Vellmere, Lior discovers her father has been printing forged conscription papers for the resistance, and that the ledger's final page bears her own true name. To finish the run of documents that will save forty families from the firing squads, she must impersonate the officer who ordered them, choose between loyalty to her father and the truth of who she is, and set the press one last time before the workshop burns. In the end, Lior surrenders the ledger to the crowd rather than let it become either weapon or inheritance, prints the town's real names openly, and claims her own name for the first time as the revolution takes the streets.
about_author: Felix Delacroix is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in provincial archives. Their novels explore the quiet people history forgets—the hands that set the type for other people's revolutions.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Lior, living as 'Lio' the apprentice, sorts type in her father Aldous's shop while imperial drums sound in the square. POV: Lior. Beat: uneasy normalcy; we learn the silences she keeps and the brother whose name she wears.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Captain Verel requisitions the town: billeting, curfew, and seizure of all civic records, including the master ledger kept in the print shop's vault. POV: Lior. Beat: dread arrives in polished boots; Aldous hands over the ledger too readily.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Lior secretly reads the ledger at night and finds debts, bribes, hidden births—and a page in her father's hand listing names marked with a printer's fist symbol. POV: Lior. Beat: curiosity curdling into fear; the shop is not what it seems.

chapters.title: The Officer Who Reads
chapters.summary: Verel returns alone, unexpectedly literate and curious about typefaces, and questions Lior about the shop's recent orders. POV: Lior. Beat: dangerous intimacy; he sees her skill but not her secret, and she almost wants him to.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Silences
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: how Lior took her brother Tam's place after his death, how her mother left, how Aldous taught her that invisibility is a craft. POV: Lior. Beat: grief explained; belonging purchased at the price of selfhood.

chapters.title: The Fist Mark
chapters.summary: Lior confronts Aldous; he admits he has been printing forged exemption papers for resistance families, funded by the ledger's hidden accounts. POV: alternating Lior and Aldous. Beat: betrayal braided with pride; loyalty vs. truth begins its argument.

chapters.title: Forty Names
chapters.summary: The resistance contact, a laundress named Maret, reveals the scope: forty families will hang unless the final run of papers is finished before the tribunal. POV: Maret. Beat: stakes made flesh; Lior is asked to cut the master plate herself.

chapters.title: Verel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Verel discovers discrepancies in the ledger and begins cross-checking names against parish records, unknowingly closing in on both the forgery ring and Lior's identity. POV: Verel. Beat: the hunter humanized; he is hunting lies because his own life was ruined by one.

chapters.title: Cutting the Plate
chapters.summary: Lior cuts the forgery plate by lamplight, her finest work ever, while Aldous grows feverish and the workshop's coal runs short. POV: Lior. Beat: artistry under terror; she realizes she is good at deception and hates it.

chapters.title: The Search
chapters.summary: Soldiers ransack the shop seeking seditious presses; Lior hides the plate inside a forme of wedding invitations and watches Verel nearly find it. POV: Lior. Beat: near-catastrophe; Verel hesitates over the invitation type and lets it pass.

chapters.title: A Name in Parish Ink
chapters.summary: Verel matches a ledger entry to a baptismal record and finds 'Lior Crane, daughter' where an apprentice should not exist—but keeps the page unsigned, uncertain why. POV: Verel. Beat: the trap half-sprung; mercy and duty begin their war inside him.

chapters.title: Maret's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maret demands the whole ledger be destroyed after the run so no one can ever be sold out again; Aldous refuses—it is his father's book, his inheritance. POV: Maret. Beat: the theme sharpened into open conflict between allies.

chapters.title: Fever Work
chapters.summary: With Aldous delirious, Lior must run the press alone through two nights, pulling proofs of the forged exemptions while the tribunal date moves closer. POV: Lior. Beat: endurance and isolation; the press becomes her only honest conversation.

chapters.title: The Uniform
chapters.summary: A dead courier's uniform arrives hidden in a paper shipment; the plan requires someone to wear it, walk into the records office, and pull the forty files before the tribunal verifies names. POV: Lior. Beat: the title lands; borrowing a life one more time.

chapters.title: Two Mirrors
chapters.summary: Lior tries on the uniform and meets Verel by chance on the street, in disguise; they speak for ten minutes, each hiding something, each recognizing something. POV: alternating Lior and Verel. Beat: doubling and recognition; the enemy becomes a mirror.

chapters.title: The Records Office
chapters.summary: Lior, in borrowed uniform, extracts the forty files under Verel's actual supervision—he knows, and says nothing, and neither understands why. POV: Lior. Beat: climax of tension; complicity replaces enmity.

chapters.title: What Verel Knows
chapters.summary: Verel's chapter: his report could end everything, but his memory of his sister erased from family records makes him burn the parish page instead. POV: Verel. Beat: the antagonist chooses truth-as-mercy over truth-as-weapon.

chapters.title: Fire in the Paper Quarter
chapters.summary: Retreating soldiers fire the district; the workshop catches, Aldous goes back for the ledger, and Lior must choose between saving him and saving the press mid-run. POV: Lior. Beat: climax; inheritance versus future, father versus work.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Lior pulls the final sheets as beams fall, Aldous dragged clear by Maret's people; the forty exemptions are printed but the ledger survives, half-burned, in her arms. POV: Lior. Beat: triumph scorched; the cost made visible.

chapters.title: The Crowd at the Door
chapters.summary: The freed town surges toward the ledger, wanting it as proof and weapon against collaborators; Lior stands between the mob and the book. POV: Lior. Beat: moral climax; loyalty to neighbors versus truth about everyone.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Instead of surrendering or burning it, Lior reads every name aloud in the square—including her own, as Lior Crane, daughter—in front of Verel, Maret, and the recovering Aldous. POV: Lior. Beat: resolution of theme; truth chosen freely ends the need for silence.

chapters.title: New Type
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in the rebuilt shop, Lior casts her first original typeface and sets a single broadside: the town's true history, signed by its author. POV: Lior. Beat: belonging earned, not borrowed; the uniform returned, the name kept.
